summary.headline: Aegis Logistics posted record H1 FY27 PAT of INR866 crore (up 108%) and agreed to buy 89.8% of Tristar Holdings for US$809 million.
summary.overview: Aegis Logistics reported Q2 FY27 revenue of INR2,213 crore (down from INR2,294 crore), with normalized segment EBITDA up 32% to INR456 crore and PAT up 32% to INR321 crore, driven by the LPG distribution margin. H1 FY27 EBITDA nearly doubled to INR1,184 crore and PAT more than doubled to INR866 crore. Aegis Vopak Terminals (AVTL) grew Q2 revenue about 17% to INR217 crore and EBITDA 22% to INR212 crore, but PAT fell to INR96 crore on higher finance costs and tax. Management also announced the signed Tristar acquisition, expected to close in Q4 FY27, and reiterated a planned ~$5 billion capex through FY30-31 at 0.6x gearing.

segments.name: LPG (Gas Division)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 EBITDA INR309 crore, +34% YoY; H1 FY27 EBITDA INR900 crore, +137% YoY. Distribution volumes 2.41 lakh MT in Q2 (+25% YoY) and 5.18 lakh MT in H1 (+54%); distribution EBITDA about INR7,000 per ton in Q2.

segments.name: Logistics (throughput)
segments.commentary: Q2 throughput 1.34 million MT, down 5% YoY but up 19% QoQ from Q1 which was hit by geopolitical disruption; sourcing volumes 0.9 lakh MT in Q2 and 2.1 lakh MT in H1 FY27.

segments.name: Liquid Division
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR187 crore (+21% YoY) and EBITDA INR147 crore (+27%); H1 revenue INR366 crore (+22%) and EBITDA INR284 crore (+28%), about 78% margin. Realization above INR3,600 per CBM on 2 million CBM storage.

segments.name: AVTL ports
segments.commentary: Q2 EBITDA margin 78.6% (+372 bps) on INR217 crore revenue; PAT lower on higher finance cost and tax. Ramp-up of recently commissioned capacity cited as revenue driver.

guidance_outlook: Tristar Holdings (89.8% stake, US$809 million, agreement signed 13 Oct 2026) expected to close in Q4 FY27, subject to regulatory approvals.
Management expects H2 FY27 to be as good as or better than H1; next update slated around end-January.
JNPT first 100,000 CBM liquid storage phase of the 318,000 CBM expansion to commission in Q3 FY27; Mumbai 64,000 CBM expansion to commission gradually this year.
Ammonia terminal at Pipavav (36,000 MT) take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc to start later this year; management sees ~INR10,000/MT revenue potential and ~INR2,750/MT storage charges.
Kochi expansion of 49,577 CBM (total 132,000 CBM) to be commissioned early FY28; Kandla CRL-4 (94,148 CBM) targeted next financial year.
Cumulative AVTL capex about USD 1.2 billion by next year; aggregate ~$5 billion planned through FY30-31, funded with equity, internal accruals and debt, targeting gearing of no more than 0.6x.
capex_capacity: JNPT greenfield expansion: ~INR1,675 crore for 318,000 CBM liquids and ~77,286 MT LPG storage; first ~100,000 CBM phase due Q3 FY27. Separate ~52,000 MT refrigerated LPG tank at JNPT announced last quarter.
JNPT LPG bottling plant (35,000 MT annual capacity) commissioned 15 Oct 2026; existing JNPT liquid storage 101,900 CBM.
Mumbai: additional 64,000 CBM liquid storage, INR125 crore, progressing on schedule.
Kandla: 952,000 CBM liquid storage and 48,000 MT static LPG; Kandla-Gorakhpur LPG pipeline (1,958 km trunk) about 96% physically complete per CRISIL; Jamnagar-Loni pipeline operational.
Mangalore: 75,000 CBM added last year now fully operational at 100% utilization, total 193,000 CBM; land secured to evaluate a further 60,000 CBM.
Haldia: additional 3 acres acquired for expansion. Pipavav ammonia terminal: 36,000 MT commissioned, built at about USD 50 million (~INR525 crore).
demand_pricing: Distribution EBITDA about INR7,000/MT in Q2, sequentially lower than Q1 which had geopolitically driven price-led margins; management attributes sustained margin to cost efficiency from larger capacity and supply chain.
Liquid realization above INR3,600/CBM; management indicated EBITDA of about INR3,000/CBM for the year, aided by high-realization JNPT and Mumbai locations.
Management claims over 30% share of India's static LPG storage capacity; logistics utilization about 25% plus on ~20 million tons of current capacity versus 29 million tons after JNPT.
Management cites a CRISIL-referenced ammonia supply-demand gap of about 3 million tons by 2029.
ITOCHU acquired 10% of Aegis Terminal Pipavav Limited and intends to raise its holding to 25% over three years.

qa_highlights.question: Integration challenges and synergies from Tristar acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tristar's ~30-year-old management will stay in place, with no operational disruption expected. Synergy details were withheld until the deal closes; qualitatively cited shared ships (about 28), inert gases, aviation refuelling and customer relationships.

qa_highlights.question: Is distribution profitability returning to about INR7,000/MT after Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 margins were price-led due to geopolitical disruption; Q2 at about INR7,000/MT reflects structural cost efficiency from larger terminals and supply-chain partnerships, which it said were earlier INR4,000-7,000 range in 2024-25.

qa_highlights.question: What is Aegis's LPG market share and LPG demand growth drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it holds more than 30% of India's static LPG capacity; demand drivers cited were income growth, shift from solid fuels and large-vessel unloading cost advantages. It said the 6 LPG terminals form a network that is hard to replicate.

qa_highlights.question: Ammonia contribution and demand clarity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a CRISIL-referenced supply-demand gap of ~3 million tons by 2029 and said it will be vertically integrated (sourcing, storage, distribution), targeting distribution margins similar to LPG and a high payback even at 25% utilization.

qa_highlights.question: Logistics volumes and capacity utilization?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 logistics throughput was 1.1 million MT and Q2 1.3 million MT (H1 about 2.4 million MT); management expects upside over the prior-year 5.1 million MT and said utilization is about 25% plus on 20 million tons current capacity.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~$5 billion capex and ~$800 million Tristar deal be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Aegis Logistics has a shareholder resolution for INR6,000 crore funding and about INR6,400 crore cash as of September, with no need for significant new debt; AVTL capex is to be funded via about $2 billion of equity raised through the IPO plus internal accruals and debt at 0.6x gearing.

risks_watch: Tristar acquisition (US$809 million, 89.8% stake) pending regulatory approvals; closing targeted Q4 FY27, and management withheld synergy quantification until completion.
Distribution EBITDA normalisation: Q2 at about INR7,000/MT versus Q1 price-led margins; management says margins are structural, but sustainability is untested.
Funding of ~$5 billion AVTL capex through FY30-31 at up to 0.6x gearing, with about $2 billion equity; AVTL PAT fell YoY on higher finance costs and tax.

Timing risk on capacity ramp-ups: JNPT first 100,000 CBM phase in Q3 FY27, ammonia take-or-pay start later this year, Kochi expansion early FY28, Kandla CRL-4 next FY, Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline ~96% complete.
Competitive intensity in LPG storage: Petronet LNG, IOCL, BPCL and JSW Infra reportedly planning new LPG capacity; management says Aegis holds more than 30% of India's static LPG capacity.
Reported figures are inconsistent in the call (AVTL Q2 revenue cited as INR217 crore and INR271 crore; H1 PAT INR165.8 crore vs INR166 crore), so the numbers need verification against filings.
key_quotes: So on the 13th of October 2026, we signed a definitive agreement to acquire 89.8% stake in Tristar Holdings Limited for a consideration of US$809 million.
So we are -- Aegis Vopak capex is self-funded by dilution of equity and listing of its shares.
We don't expect to change the management and the continuity will ensure that there is no disturbance in the operations and performance of the company.
So we hold more than 30% of the static capacity of LPG in the country.
The second half of the year promises to be as good, if not better.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on operations, with Murad Moledina calling Q2 a "perfect quarter" and management guiding H2 FY27 to be as good as or better than H1. Cautious and evasive on Tristar, repeatedly declining to quantify synergies or deal detail before closing, and reticent on market-share and LPG pricing specifics.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: AVTL Q2 EBITDA margin 78.6% (+372 bps YoY) and H1 margin 77.7%; Liquid EBITDA guided at about INR3,000/CBM this year, and management expects H2 FY27 to be as good as or better than H1, though distribution margin normalises from Q1 price-led levels to about INR7,000/MT in Q2.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: JNPT first 100,000 CBM phase of 318,000 CBM due Q3 FY27, Mumbai 64,000 CBM commissioning this year, ammonia terminal take-or-pay start later this year, Kochi 49,577 CBM early FY28, Kandla CRL-4 94,148 CBM next FY; Mangalore 75,000 CBM already at 100% utilisation.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Logistics throughput 1.34 million MT in Q2 (+19% QoQ) with management expecting upside over prior-year 5.1 million MT; LPG distribution volumes 2.41 lakh MT in Q2 (+25% YoY) and H1 +54%, and utilisation about 25%+ on ~20 million tons capacity.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Aggregate ~$5 billion AVTL capex through FY30-31 already planned with cumulative ~$1.2 billion by FY28, and utilisation at 100% at Mangalore with land secured for a further 60,000 CBM, so further capex announcements are firmly in motion.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides H2 FY27 as good as or better than H1 (H1 Aegis Logistics PAT INR866 crore, +108% YoY), but Tristar synergies are withheld and Q2 AVTL PAT fell to INR96 crore, so an explicit upgrade is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Distribution EBITDA normalising from Q1 price-led margins to about INR7,000/MT in Q2, AVTL PAT down YoY (INR96 crore vs INR100 crore) on higher finance cost and tax, and capacity ramp-up timing risk on JNPT, Kochi and Kandla.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pipavav ammonia terminal (36,000 MT) take-or-pay start later this year, management seeing ~INR10,000/MT revenue potential and a CRISIL-cited ~3 million ton ammonia supply-demand gap by 2029; JNPT LPG bottling plant (35,000 MT) commissioned 15 Oct 2026.

rows.label: Tristar Holdings acquisition (89.8%, US$809 million)
rows.why: Signed 13 Oct 2026 and expected to close in Q4 FY27 subject to regulatory approvals; synergy quantification withheld until close, and Aegis Logistics has INR6,400 crore cash as of September.

rows.label: AVTL equity raise (~$2 billion via IPO) to fund capex
rows.why: Management says ~$2 billion of equity raised through the IPO plus internal accruals and debt will fund ~$5 billion capex at gearing of no more than 0.6x; AVTL PAT fell YoY on higher finance costs.

rows.label: ITOCHU raising stake in Aegis Terminal Pipavav to 25%
rows.why: ITOCHU acquired 10% of Aegis Terminal Pipavav and intends to raise its holding to 25% over three years, a stated plan with a timeline.

tone.note: Management was confident on LPG distribution, liquid storage utilisation (Mangalore at 100%) and H2 FY27 guidance, but cautious and evasive on Tristar synergies and deal detail; analysts pushed on the sustainability of the ~INR7,000/MT distribution margin after Q1 and the funding of the ~$5 billion
